stem.text: Let p be a continuous function with \( \int_{-1}^{2} p(x)\,dx = -2 \) and \( \int_{4}^{2} p(x)\,dx = -8 \). Find the value of \( \int_{4}^{-1} \left(2p(x) - 3\right) dx \).

worked_solution.text: Join the adjacent intervals: \( \int_{-1}^{4} p(x)\,dx = \int_{-1}^{2} p(x)\,dx + \int_{2}^{4} p(x)\,dx = -2 + (8) = 6 \), since reversing \( \int_{4}^{2} \) changes its sign.
Reverse the requested integral: \( \int_{4}^{-1} \left(2p(x) - 3\right) dx = -(2) \int_{-1}^{4} p(x)\,dx + (-3)(-1 - 4) \), and the constant contributes \( 15 \).

difficulty_variables.whether a reversal of limits is required: yes, both a supplied integral and the requested one run right to left
difficulty_variables.whether a constant multiple or a sum app: constant multiple plus a constant term

distractor_derivations.A: sign change for the reversed target integral left out
distractor_derivations.B: given integral from 4 to 2 used as if it ran from 2 to 4
distractor_derivations.D: constant term integrated as if its limits ran left to right, so its sign change is left out
